newsitem.title: USA: HDS to change name, makes Hitachi deal.
newsitem.headline: HDS to change name, makes Hitachi deal.

text.p: HDS Network Systems said Tuesday it plans to change its name to Neoware Systems Inc and its symbol to NWRE on Aug. 1.
In a separate release, the company said Hitachi Data Systems agreed to license the company's netOS operating system and purchase versions of its network computers.
Hitachi Data Systems, based in Santa Clara, Calif., is owned by Hitachi Ltd and Electronic Data Systems Corp.
The new name aims to reflect the company's focus on network computer technology. The company makes network computers as well as the netOS operating system software.
Network computers are stripped-down, inexpensive computers without their own memory or disk drive that offer easy access to the Internet, e-mail and other networks.

Hitachi will buy versions of the workStation and NeoStation network computers and the netOS operating system for resale to its customers as part of Hitachi Data Systems' multi-vendor integration program.
Also, HDS said it assigned all rights and title to the name HDS to Hitachi Data Systems, including the hds.com web domain name. Terms of the deals were not disclosed.
